title: CCL Products (India) Ltd - 519600 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.76% to INR1,203.59 crore on ~20% volume growth, with EBITDA up 21.84% to INR196.69 crore and net debt cut to INR963 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 turnover was INR1,203.59 crore (up 13.76% YoY) on roughly 20% volume growth, with coffee price pass-through muting top-line growth. EBITDA rose 21.84% to INR196.69 crore and PAT rose 61.31% to INR116.87 crore. Net debt fell to INR963 crore from INR1,073 crore at March 2026, and management reiterated 15% full-year volume guidance without upgrading it. Management said EBITDA per kg (about INR140, per analyst question) should hold for FY27, and standalone margins were hit by logistics and packaging cost increases.

financial_highlights.change: down from INR1,073 crore at March 2026, about INR100 crore QoQ reduction
term loan INR517 crore, working capital INR751 crore

financial_highlights.value: INR180 crore total, of which about INR125 crore branded

segments.name: Coffee B2B (contract manufacturing, cost-plus)
segments.commentary: Volume growth about 20% in Q1 against 15% full-year guidance; revenue growth of 13.76% lagged volume because of lower green coffee prices (INR3,300-3,800 per kg range cited). Capacity utilisation about 65-70% in aggregate, with freeze-dried running higher than spray-dried.

segments.name: Domestic branded B2C
segments.commentary: Gross turnover about INR180 crore, of which about INR125 crore branded, with Q1 growth about 26% YoY. Management targets INR550-600 crore branded sales in FY27 and 25-30% B2C growth; domestic EBITDA margin held at 5-6% to fund growth. Share claims: above 6% urban share in South India, double-digit share at Reliance and DMart, and very high single digits on quick commerce.

segments.name: International B2C (Percol UK)
segments.commentary: Percol UK turned around; FY26 top line about INR26-27 crore. Distributor talks under way in the US and Middle East, with some deals expected to close in a couple of months.

segments.name: Malgudi snacks
segments.commentary: Broader rollout began about 5-6 days before the call, with banana chips added to chegodi and murukku; management expects only a couple of crore of revenue in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 volume growth guidance of 15% reiterated, not upgraded despite 20% Q1 growth; management cited client wait-and-watch amid coffee volatility.
EBITDA per kg to stay around current levels (about INR140) for FY27; EBITDA growth expected to track volume growth.
Domestic branded volume growth of 20-25% in FY27 and branded sales of INR550-600 crore, with margins kept at 5-6% EBITDA rather than harvested.
FY27 capex of INR25-50 crore, mainly upgrades and additions to existing lines; no major capacity expansion planned for the next 2-3 years.
Gross debt to fall by about INR100 crore to around INR1,000 crore, and net debt to around INR800 crore; FY27 term loan repayment about INR200 crore.
Volume growth of about 15% sustained for the next 3-4 years, with B2C growing 25-30%.
capex_capacity: Total rated capacity about 77,000 tonnes; Vietnam rated capacity about 36,000 (figure raised by analyst, not disputed); India and Vietnam both run at similar utilisation of about 65-70%.
Freeze-dried utilisation is higher than spray-dried, and freeze-dried share is up YoY; management says spray-dried still carries larger volumes.
Management plans new capacity at 75-85% utilisation, with 9-12 months lead time for brownfield additions in India and Vietnam.
Parent-company capacity has been flat for more than 10 years; future volume growth will come mainly from subsidiaries.
Management said freeze-dried capex is only taken on with firm demand conviction because of high capex and 24/7 operation; no freeze-dried capex is currently in the books for the next 2 years.
demand_pricing: Green coffee prices around INR3,300-3,800 per kg; management sees volatility from Brazil supply versus El Nino risk to the Vietnam crop due in Nov-Dec.
Cost-plus model: margins are not affected by coffee price moves, and the rupee is naturally hedged with forex policies; a rupee depreciation can squeeze margins.
Freeze-dried earns about 30-40% more EBITDA than spray-dried, per management's rule of thumb.
Distribution margins now 5-6% for CCL against 4-5% for large FMCG peers; retailer margin about 10%. 70% of branded business is cash-and-carry.
Logistics and packaging costs were volatile in Q1 on Middle East disruption, with some cost pressure absorbed; CCL's Middle East exposure is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Can 15% volume growth continue given coffee volatility and rupee depreciation, and will margins benefit from depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 15% volume guidance without upgrading. It said a forex policy covers appreciation, and that EBITDA growth will track volume growth on a cost-plus basis.

qa_highlights.question: Will capacity constrain growth beyond FY28 at 95%+ utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity will not hinder growth. Expansion is considered at 75-85% utilisation, with 9-12 months lead time, and the company is willing to use tie-ups.

qa_highlights.question: Is EBITDA per kg likely to rise further, and why was Q1 lower historically?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided EBITDA per kg to hold for FY27. It said seasonality is limited and the historical Q1 dip was likely coincidence or mix-driven.

qa_highlights.question: What is the domestic market share, and when will the branded business turn PAT-positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Urban share in South India is above 6%, with double-digit share in Reliance and DMart. Management does not report PAT for the domestic business separately and is keeping EBITDA at 5-6% to fund growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the debt repayment and cash deployment plans?
qa_highlights.answer: INR140 crore of term loan falls due over the next three quarters, with about INR200 crore in FY28 and the balance in FY29. Management said cash flows will not repeat the FY26 INR858 crore level. Acquisitions are being considered only where distribution can be leveraged.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone performance weaker than consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to logistics costs, small-pack packaging price increases, and the high base of the prior-year standalone quarter. It said the standalone business is in line with Q4 FY26.

risks_watch: Coffee price volatility (Brazil supply versus El Nino risk to Vietnam crop due Nov-Dec) and possible client wait-and-watch on contracts.
Logistics and packaging cost inflation tied to Middle East disruption, hitting standalone margins.
Rupee depreciation squeezing the import-export margin spread despite the forex policy.
Capacity utilisation rising toward 85-90% with no committed expansion; the next capacity decision is due in 1-2 years.
Slow rollout of Malgudi snacks and new markets (North, West) for branded growth.
Gross debt of INR1,268 crore and working capital intensity (166 days) limit free cash flow conversion.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth, deleveraging, and brand metrics, but guarded on coffee price and logistics direction. Management declined to comment on peer EBITDA per kg and gave few volume-split details, citing the 'wait and watch' stance.
key_quotes: We work on a cost-plus model, and our focus always is on the volume growth.
There isn't much of a -- yes, there will be an impact owing to the dip in the import and the export prices, which is the margin that you earn upon.
We will never let capacity hinder our growth.
Going forward also, majority of the growth will start coming in from the subsidiary companies only.

growth.why: Management reiterated 15% FY27 volume growth (not upgraded despite ~20% Q1 volume), branded sales target INR550-600 crore with 25-30% B2C growth, backed by demand and distribution claims but no new capacity for 2-3 years, with utilisation at 65-70% and capex only INR25-50 crore.
